claims.text: The intervention is a 5-micrometer-thick Al2O3 surface coating applied to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by plasma spraying.
The relevant oxidation exposure is 1000 °C for 100 hours in air.
The alumina coating will improve the oxidation resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by 90% relative to the untreated alloy under the specified exposure.
The coating will limit the reduction in room-temperature yield strength to no more than 10%.
Plasma-sprayed alumina will form a dense, protective oxide scale on HfNbTaTiZr.
The dense alumina scale will prevent oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Preventing oxygen diffusion into the alloy will produce the predicted improvement in oxidation resistance.
Poor oxidation resistance is an obstacle to the high-temperature engineering use of refractory high-entropy alloys.
A Cr-containing WVTaTiCr refractory high-entropy-alloy coating can exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation resistance and high hardness as Cr content increases.
The magnitude of oxidation improvement and yield-strength retention may depend on the coating process.
The magnitude of oxidation improvement and yield-strength retention may depend on the alloy microstructure.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis permits no more than a 10% yield-strength loss, but the experiment only falsifies it for a loss greater than 15%, leaving outcomes above the claimed boundary but at or below 15% non-falsifying.
